sourceClaims: A function is a named, reusable block of code defined with def that runs only when it is called; variables created inside it are local to that call.

A variable created outside any function has global scope and can be accessed anywhere in the program.

sourceClaims: Silicate minerals, built from the silicon-oxygen tetrahedron, are the most abundant rock-forming minerals; the way tetrahedra link together defines the major silicate structures.
The silicon-oxygen tetrahedron (SiO4) is one silicon atom at the center bonded to four oxygen atoms at the corners.
Tetrahedra link by sharing corner oxygen atoms into chains, sheets, or three-dimensional frameworks.
How much oxygen is shared between tetrahedra controls the silicate group — isolated tetrahedra, single chains, sheets, or frameworks like quartz.

originalTerm.df: Rock formed when molten material cools quickly at or near the Earth's surface.
originalTerm.mi: Rock formed by slow cooling deep within the crust.
originalTerm.cx: Rock formed by rapid cooling at or near the surface.

sourceClaims: Igneous rock forms when molten magma or lava cools and crystallizes; how fast it cools controls crystal size, distinguishing coarse intrusive rocks from fine-grained extrusive rocks.
Lava cooling quickly at the surface forms tiny crystals, while magma cooling slowly at depth forms large crystals.
Magma that cools slowly deep within the crust forms intrusive (plutonic) rock with a coarse-grained texture.
Lava cooling at or near the surface forms extrusive (volcanic) rock with a fine-grained texture.

originalTerm.df: A sequence of chords that forms the foundation of harmony in Western musical tradition.
originalTerm.eg: The progression of i, iv, and v chords in the key of A minor (A minor, D minor, E minor).
originalTerm.mi: A single chord used repeatedly throughout a piece.
originalTerm.cx: A sequence of chords that forms the foundation of harmony in Western musical tradition.

sourceClaims: In music, harmony is the concept of combining different sounds in order to create new, distinct musical ideas.
In these genres, chord progressions are the defining feature on which melody and rhythm are built.
Chord progressions are the foundation of harmony in Western musical tradition from the common practice era of classical music to the 21st century.
A first chord forms a 'progression' with a second chord, and a second with a third.
For example, the relative minor of C major is A minor, and in the key of A minor, the i, iv and v chords are A minor, D minor and E minor.
In many styles of popular and traditional music, chord progressions are expressed using the name and "quality" of the chords.
